attacks.claim: Pickup codes are sent in plaintext SMS and the code alone is not a credential. Compromise of the phone (SIM swap, shared or lost device) exposes a live pickup code to a second factor.
attacks.evidence: "Code 482913, pick up by Sat Nov 14" and "enters card number + PIN, existing ILS PIN lockout applies"

attacks.claim: The SMS provider retains message logs for 30 days. Those logs contain the patron's phone number, hold location and live locker code, but the DPA was signed in 2025-03, before this data flow existed, and the artifact does not show it covers hold or pickup data.
attacks.evidence: "it retains message logs 30 days and is barred from marketing use" / "our existing DPA (signed 2025-03)"

attacks.claim: SMS delivery depends on one provider, with the 10DLC brand and campaign registered to it, and lockers depend on one vendor with no described exit or alternative path. Switching cost is not addressed.
attacks.evidence: "the SMS provider is an existing vendor" / "campaign CX7R2Q" / "vendor SLA 4 h on-site"

attacks.claim: Enabling for all ~210k cardholders on day one, with every queued quiet-hours message released at 08:00, creates a single-timestep burst. The artifact gives no throughput, carrier rate-limit or load-test evidence for that burst.
attacks.evidence: "anything later is queued to 08:00" / "flags on for all cardholders"

attacks.claim: When the SMS cap trips, every opted-in patron falls back to automated phone calls, a channel with no budget, rate or cap. The $900 cap bounds SMS spend only, so total spend is not bounded.
attacks.evidence: "texts stop and every opted-in patron falls back to their previous notice method (email or automated phone call"

attacks.claim: A locker bank offline for up to 4 h (vendor SLA) leaves patrons directed to an unavailable locker with no per-locker reroute, and the artifact gives no mechanism to change pickup location for that window.
attacks.evidence: "any locker bank offline > 10 min (pages branch manager + vendor; vendor SLA 4 h on-site)"

attacks.claim: On permanent SMS withdrawal, consent records are deleted within 30 days. Those records are the evidence needed to defend consent claims, so the rollback destroys proof of consent.
attacks.evidence: "numbers and consent records are deleted within 30 days and patrons are emailed"

attacks.claim: Batching extra holds into one text shows one location, one code and one deadline. Holds at different branches, cells or deadlines cannot be represented, so a patron could miss a hold or go to the wrong locker.
attacks.evidence: "extra holds are batched into one message" / "2 holds ready at Oak St locker. Code 482913, pick up by Sat Nov 14"

attacks.claim: The QA summary reports results from a staff pilot scheduled for Nov 2–6, but today is 2026-10-26, so those results cannot exist yet. The provider was also tested in test mode, so real carrier delivery is unproven.
attacks.evidence: "Staff pilot week (64 staff cards, real holds) | 0 misdelivered texts" vs "Nov 2-6: flags on for staff cards only (pilot above)" / "against the production SMS provider account in test mode"

attacks.claim: Nothing found for this lens beyond the announcement wording, which is covered under ux-value.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no rendering or layout defect identified in the artifact text

attacks.claim: The announcement says 'every cardholder' can get text alerts, but juvenile cards are excluded and see no option, so the public message overstates the feature.
attacks.evidence: "Text alerts for holds, for every cardholder."

attacks.claim: The opt-in requires a separate YES reply before any text is sent, and how a patron selects a locker versus a desk pickup is not described, which adds friction.
attacks.evidence: "texts start only after the patron replies YES" / "pickup_location" assignment not described

attacks.claim: Locker pickup is touchscreen-only, with audio available only through a headphone jack and no tactile keypad described. Outside opening hours there is no accessible alternative, so blind or low-vision patrons cannot collect holds unaided at night.
attacks.evidence: "screen has high-contrast mode, audio guidance through a headphone jack" / "Holds stay collectible at the service desk during opening hours"

attacks.claim: Teen (13–17) cards can opt in to SMS on their own phone with no guardian consent step, and the artifact does not show LGL-118 covers minors. Minor-consent and state library-confidentiality exposure is unaddressed.
attacks.evidence: "The option appears on adult and teen (13+) cards only" / "legal review complete (ticket LGL-118)"

attacks.claim: The remap SQL was tested on 1,200 rows, far below production locker-hold volume, and the claim that QA used prod flags 'verbatim' conflicts with the $5 test spend cap, so the cap path is not tested with production values.
attacks.evidence: "tested in staging on 1,200 rows" / "copied verbatim" with "(test cap $5)"

attacks.claim: Monitoring has no alert on fallback-channel volume (phone calls), queue backlog or STOP-rate spikes, so the cost and opt-out risks above would go unnoticed.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: alerts for fallback volume, queue depth or STOP-rate thresholds

attacks.claim: The QA table reports results from the staff pilot as completed, but the rollout section schedules that pilot for Nov 2-6, after the current date of 2026-10-26. The pilot evidence cannot exist yet, so the table is either premature or misdated.
attacks.evidence: Staff pilot week (64 staff cards, real holds) | 0 misdelivered texts; 2 copy fixes shipped and re-verified  vs  1. Nov 2-6: flags on for staff cards only (pilot above).

attacks.claim: The approved public announcement says every cardholder gets text alerts. That contradicts the opt-in design and the juvenile-card exclusion, so it is a misleading public claim about a consent-based service.
attacks.evidence: Announcement text says exactly: "Text alerts for holds, for every cardholder." vs "The option appears on adult and teen (13+) cards only; juvenile cards do not show it"

attacks.claim: The pickup credential (locker code) is sent to whatever phone number is on the account. Nothing requires re-authentication when the number is changed, so an attacker with portal credentials could add their own number, confirm with YES, and receive codes. Card or card+PIN is still needed at the locker, but a portal takeover could make collection feasible.
attacks.evidence: "Phone field" plus "texts start only after the patron replies YES"; ABSENT: step-up verification or notice to the old number on phone change

attacks.claim: The rollback assumes SMS-only patrons still get email, but the opt-in allows SMS 'instead of' email, so email may be suppressed. The fallback path was tested only for the spend cap, not for SMS-only patrons.
attacks.evidence: "in addition to (or instead of) the current email" vs "every opted-in patron gets hold notices by their previous method (email or automated phone call, kept on file)"

attacks.claim: The approved budget (~$460/month) covers SMS only. The $900 cap applies only to the SMS provider, while the fallback sends automated phone calls for every opted-in patron, which are unbudgeted and have no stated cap. The worst case is uncapped voice spend.
attacks.evidence: "Forecast 38,000 texts/month ... ~$460/month" and "Provider account hard spend cap $900/month ... every opted-in patron falls back to their previous notice method (email or automated phone call"

attacks.claim: The 38,000 texts/month forecast has no stated basis such as an opt-in rate or hold volume. Pilot evidence is 64 staff cards on a provider test account, so delivery and volume at 210k cardholders is unvalidated.
attacks.evidence: "Forecast 38,000 texts/month at about $0.012" vs "production SMS provider account in test mode" and "Staff pilot week (64 staff cards"

attacks.claim: All overnight-queued texts release at 08:00, and flags go on for all 210k cardholders at 09:00 on launch day. This creates a synchronized burst of confirmations and notices with no stated rate limiting, provider throughput check, or load test at production scale.
attacks.evidence: "anything later is queued to 08:00" and "Nov 9 09:00: flags on for all cardholders"; ABSENT: load or throughput test

attacks.claim: The message format is ambiguous for batched holds. One code is shown for two holds, yet codes are described as single-use. It is also unclear how batching behaves when holds span different lockers or include desk pickups.
attacks.evidence: "2 holds ready at Oak St locker. Code 482913" vs "Codes are single-use" and "extra holds are batched into one message"

attacks.claim: The locker interface is touchscreen-only with no tactile keypad described, and the QA table includes no accessibility test for the locker. Audio guidance and high contrast are claimed but not verified.
attacks.evidence: "Touchscreen and card reader mounted ... audio guidance through a headphone jack"; QA rows for locker: card+code, card number+PIN+code, wrong code x5 only; ABSENT: locker screen-reader or low-vision test

attacks.claim: The consent record retention period is not stated, and it is unclear whether the phone number and IP are deleted or kept after STOP. STOP only clears the opt-in flag.
attacks.evidence: "consent record (timestamp, IP, checkbox text version) are stored in the patron record" vs "STOP ... clears the opt-in flag"

attacks.claim: Lock-screen previews would show a library name, hold count, and a valid locker code. The provider also keeps message bodies, including codes, for 30 days.
attacks.evidence: "Riverbend Library: 2 holds ready at Oak St locker. Code 482913, pick up by Sat Nov 14"; provider "retains message logs 30 days"

attacks.claim: Five wrong code attempts lock a cell, and clearing the lock needs staff. Someone holding a valid card and PIN could repeatedly lock cells, especially after hours.
attacks.evidence: "5 wrong attempts lock the cell and alert branch staff"

attacks.claim: There is a single SMS provider, with no stated data residency for phone numbers or logs and no described exit path beyond deleting data on withdrawal.
attacks.evidence: "The SMS provider is covered by our existing DPA (signed 2025-03)"; "If SMS is withdrawn permanently, numbers and consent records are deleted"

attacks.claim: Outside opening hours, a locker bank that goes offline has a 4-hour vendor SLA, while the service is advertised as 24/7 and the SMS code points only to the locker.
attacks.evidence: "vendor SLA 4 h on-site" and "24/7 pickup lockers"

attacks.claim: The text directs patrons only to the locker. Patrons who want desk pickup have no path from the message, which conflicts with the stated option to collect at the desk.
attacks.evidence: "Holds stay collectible at the service desk during opening hours for anyone who prefers it" vs "2 holds ready at Oak St locker"

attacks.claim: The Spanish disclosure and Spanish message are not shown, so consent validity for Spanish-language patrons cannot be checked from the artifact.
attacks.evidence: "English and Spanish, following the patron's existing language preference"; only the English disclosure and message are quoted

attacks.claim: The locker-to-desk remap was tested only on 1,200 rows, with no stated production volume, so the rollback's manual staff workload at three branches is unknown.
attacks.evidence: "scripts/remap_locker_holds.sql (tested in staging on 1,200 rows)"

attacks.claim: The opt-out wording is inconsistent between the disclosure and the message.
attacks.evidence: "Reply STOP to cancel" vs "Reply STOP to opt out"

attacks.claim: No blocking issue found: the feature addresses a clear patron need, with the desk path retained as a fallback.
attacks.evidence: "Holds stay collectible at the service desk during opening hours"

attacks.claim: The 3-texts-per-day cap and batching are reasonable, but worst-case spend is high before the hard cap triggers.
attacks.evidence: "Max 3 texts per patron per day"

attacks.claim: No additional gate-worthy issue found beyond the attacks above.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: nothing further in artifact text

attacks.claim: Rollback deletes numbers and consent records within 30 days if SMS is withdrawn, and the notification log is purged at 30 days. No retention period is set for proof of opt-in, so the library may be unable to show consent if a patron later disputes a text.
attacks.evidence: "If SMS is withdrawn permanently, numbers and consent records are deleted within 30 days and patrons are emailed."

attacks.claim: The $900/month cap covers only the SMS provider. When it trips, every opted-in patron falls back to automated phone calls, which are not in the $460 forecast, not budgeted, and not capped. The fallback can add unbounded spend exactly when the SMS budget is exhausted.
attacks.evidence: "On cap, texts stop and every opted-in patron falls back to their previous notice method (email or automated phone call, which stays on file)"

attacks.claim: The announcement tells all cardholders they will get texts, which contradicts the opt-in flow and the juvenile-card exclusion. Public copy that overstates who receives texts is a consent and misleading-communication risk.
attacks.evidence: "Text alerts for holds, for every cardholder." versus "The option appears on adult and teen (13+) cards only; juvenile cards do not show it"

attacks.claim: Teen (13+) cardholders can opt in to texts with their own phone, so the library collects and texts minors' numbers with no guardian consent path. The exclusion covers only juvenile cards.
attacks.evidence: "The option appears on adult and teen (13+) cards only; juvenile cards do not show it, and guardians can opt in with their own number on the linked guardian account."

attacks.claim: The carrier and STOP results cannot be true under the stated setup. The provider account was in test mode, which does not send real carrier traffic, so 10DLC delivery, carrier filtering and STOP handling on four real carriers were not validated in production.
attacks.evidence: "against the production SMS provider account in test mode" alongside "Opt-in, YES confirm, STOP, HELP, re-opt-in (EN + ES) on 4 carriers | Pass"

attacks.claim: The single-use locker unlock code is sent in plaintext SMS and stays valid until the pickup deadline, up to several days. Anyone with access to the phone, a shared device, or a notification preview can read it and combine it with the card number to open the locker.
attacks.evidence: "2 holds ready at Oak St locker. Code 482913, pick up by Sat Nov 14."

attacks.claim: The locker touchscreen features (high-contrast mode, headphone audio guidance, adjustable text size, reach height) are claimed but have no QA result. Screen-reader and keyboard testing covers only the opt-in web form, not the locker kiosk.
attacks.evidence: "Touchscreen and card reader mounted within ADA reach range (max 48 in); screen has high-contrast mode, audio guidance through a headphone jack, and adjustable text size." versus QA rows covering only "Opt-in form with NVDA + Firefox, VoiceOver iOS; 320/768/1280 px layouts"

attacks.claim: The text shows the patron's hold count and locker location to anyone who sees the phone. That is borrowing-activity exposure, and it sits uneasily with the claim that texts carry no item counts.
attacks.evidence: "No titles, authors or item counts by format appear in any text." versus "2 holds ready at Oak St locker."

attacks.claim: Retention for the phone number and consent record (including IP address) after a patron sends STOP or is removed is not specified. Only the notification log has a stated purge period.
attacks.evidence: "Phone number and consent record (timestamp, IP, checkbox text version) are stored in the patron record" with no retention period given

attacks.claim: Alerts do not cover queue backlog, which can build overnight for 08:00 release, or failure of the email/call fallback path. The fallback could fail silently.
attacks.evidence: "Alerts: delivery failures > 5% for 15 min, webhook signature failures > 0, any locker bank offline > 10 min"

attacks.claim: Flags go on for all cardholders at once on a Monday morning, with no stated send-rate plan or 10DLC throughput check for roughly 210k eligible patrons. Queued texts could bunch into a single 08:00 burst.
attacks.evidence: "Nov 9 09:00: flags on for all cardholders"

attacks.claim: Whether a patron who opts in to SMS still receives the email notice is ambiguous. If both are sent, patrons may get duplicate notices, and the pickup code could be sent twice.
attacks.evidence: "in addition to (or instead of) the current email"

attacks.claim: The locker rollback script was validated only on 1,200 staging rows. Production remapping volume, deadline extensions and patron notices are untested at scale.
attacks.evidence: "scripts/remap_locker_holds.sql (tested in staging on 1,200 rows)"
